points: Claude makes visuals by writing code without seeing the result. SVG maps closely to the picture because every element has coordinates; with HTML and CSS the layout comes out of flexbox, grid, the cascade and font metrics, which Claude has to predict. That's where spacing goes off and things overflow.
What helps any session: a reference screenshot or a design system, a render-screenshot-fix loop, and a specific look ('dense, editorial, high contrast') rather than just the content.
A great one-shot artifact is Opus on a blank canvas. In your repos, screens are built by Sonnet by rule, checked for compliance not feel, with polish tools off and the screenshot loop optional.
Plan runs on Opus but writes steps, files, risks and checks in under 25 lines. It can't write files and never loads frontend-design or ux/, so every visual decision falls to the Sonnet builder.
Design-review's blind reviewers run on Haiku in round 1 (agents/reviewer.md). Rounds escalate only on a FAIL, so a flat screen that passes is never looked at again.
frontend-design loads only for a new screen or a repo with no design yet. impeccable's build commands (polish, layout, animate, bolder, delight) are refused by the guard rule impeccable-review-only.
No browser MCP is configured anywhere, and claude-settings does not install Playwright (banchi and q_max bring their own). In solo mode, styling-only edits merge on passing checks alone.
Word pressure: STE020 refuses button or label text over 4 words, and the fewest-words decision says it counts most in front-end work. There is no house icon set to fall back on.
Across repos, screens that started from a mockup came out polished (banchi's #/gallery, q_max's home page, home-app's SpeakerSheet). The rest drift.

How design-review is built: reviewer A checks the pinned Vercel web-interface rules plus your house checklist; reviewer B runs impeccable's audit and critique. Both are blind to the repo's design records; the orchestrator compares afterwards, and any clash goes to you. Nothing in it builds, and both reviewers inherit the reviewer agent's Haiku model.
summary: The core diagnosis behind the Design phase.
title: Why UI quality swings
